terms.gloss: the voice of a verb: active or passive
evidence: Quint. 1.4.27: sed in verbīs quoque quis est adeō imperītus, ut ignōret genera
terms.comment: With verbs genus is voice, as with nouns it is gender: Cujus generis est? Āctīvī an passīvī?, what voice is it? Active or passive? (Traupman 241). Quintilian also says modus: patiendī modus, the passive, faciendī, the active (9.3.7).

phrases.latin: sed in verbīs quoque quis est adeō imperītus, ut ignōret genera et quālitātēs et persōnās et numerōs?
phrases.english: but in verbs too, who is so ignorant as not to know voices, moods, persons and numbers?
How many voices of verbs are there?

sources: Lewis & Short: genus · Lewis & Short: modus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 227, p. 241, p. 244, p. 249.
